scene: SKIP: replacement needs a before and an after; one picture of an apple and a pushed-away banana reads as a choice or as two fruits, not as one thing taking the place of another.
example_nl: Ik drink thee in plaats van koffie.
example_en: I drink tea instead of coffee.

scene: the adult sits on a bench on the open deck of a small plain ferry sailing on wave lines, seen side-on, the suitcase on the lap, a lifebuoy on the rail and three speed lines behind the hull. No wings, no runway and no quay are in the picture.
must: a seated adult on the deck of a ferry sailing on waves.
avoid: an adult behind a round window of a plane in the sky (met het vliegtuig); an adult in a rowing boat on a lake (not the card); an adult walking up a gangplank (not the card); a bridge over a river (not the card).
contrast: Pair with met-het-vliegtuig. The only difference is the vehicle: a ferry sailing on waves here, a plane flying in the sky there.
example_nl: Wij gaan met de boot.
example_en: We go by boat.
alt: Een man zit met een koffer op het dek van een schip dat over de golven vaart.

scene: the adult sits behind one of a row of small round windows of a plain passenger plane flying level in an empty sky, the suitcase on the lap, two wings, a tail fin, the wheels tucked away and three speed lines behind it. No water is in the picture.
must: a seated adult behind a round window of a plane in the sky.
avoid: an adult on the deck of a ferry on waves (met de boot); an adult climbing boarding steps (not the card); a helicopter (not the card); a hot-air balloon (not the card).
contrast: Pair with met-de-boot. The only difference is the vehicle: a plane flying in the sky here, a ferry sailing on waves there.
example_nl: Zij reist met het vliegtuig.
example_en: She travels by plane.
alt: Een vrouw zit met een koffer achter een rond raampje van een toestel met vleugels hoog in de lucht.

scene: the three cups stand in one straight horizontal line across the table from left to right, each a small gap from the next, all handles pointing the same way. No cup is in front of or on top of another.
must: three cups in a line from left to right.
avoid: three cups in a column going away from the viewer (achter elkaar); three cups stacked in a tower (op elkaar); three cups scattered at random (not the card); three cups in a triangle (not the card).
contrast: Pair with achter-elkaar and op-elkaar. The only difference is the arrangement: a row across the picture here, a column into the picture or a tower there.
example_nl: Wij lopen naast elkaar naar school.
example_en: We walk to school side by side.
alt: Drie gelijke bekers staan in een rij van links naar rechts met kleine tussenruimtes.

scene: the three cups stand in one straight line that runs away from the viewer toward the back of the table, the nearest cup the largest and the farthest the smallest, each a small gap behind the previous. The line is the same width as one cup.
must: three cups going away into the picture, nearest largest.
avoid: three cups in a line across the picture (naast elkaar); three cups stacked in a tower (op elkaar); three cups in a triangle (not the card); three cars driving in a line (not the card).
contrast: Pair with naast-elkaar and op-elkaar. The only difference is the arrangement: a column into the picture here, a row across it or a tower there.
example_nl: De auto's rijden achter elkaar.
example_en: The cars drive one behind the other.
alt: Drie gelijke bekers staan in een smalle rij die van de kijker af loopt, de dichtste het grootst.

scene: the three cups are stacked in a tower, each one standing on top of the one below with the handles pointing the same way and the tower slightly wobbly, rising to three times the height of one cup. The table is otherwise empty.
must: three cups piled one on top of the other.
avoid: three cups in a row across the table (naast elkaar); three cups in a column going away (achter elkaar); three cups in a heap fallen over (not the card); a cup on a shelf above another cup (not the card).
contrast: Pair with naast-elkaar and achter-elkaar. The only difference is the arrangement: a tower here, a row across or a column into the picture there.
example_nl: De borden staan op elkaar.
example_en: The plates are stacked on top of each other.
alt: Drie gelijke bekers vormen een kleine toren op het tafelblad.

scene: the adult stands still with both feet together on the top landing beside the door, body turned to the viewer and one hand on the end of the handrail. All seven steps below are empty down to the floor line.
must: a person standing still on the top landing, every step below empty.
avoid: a person standing still on the floor at the foot (onderaan de trap); a person halfway down facing the floor (not the card); a person halfway up facing the door (not the card); a person on a balcony (not the card).
contrast: Pair with onderaan-de-trap, naar-boven and naar-beneden. The only difference is the adult: standing still on the top landing here, standing still on the floor, or halfway up or down there.
example_nl: De kat zit bovenaan de trap.
example_en: The cat is sitting at the top of the stairs.
alt: Een vrouw staat stil op de hoogste vloer naast een deur; alle treden lager zijn leeg.

scene: the adult stands still with both feet together on the floor line at the foot of the staircase, body turned to the viewer and one hand on the post of the handrail. All seven steps up to the landing and its door are empty.
must: a person standing still on the floor at the foot, every step empty.
avoid: a person standing still on the top landing (bovenaan de trap); a person halfway up facing the door (not the card); a person halfway down facing the floor (not the card); a person sitting on the first step (not the card).
contrast: Pair with bovenaan-de-trap, naar-boven and naar-beneden. The only difference is the adult: standing still on the floor here, standing still on the landing, or halfway up or down there.
example_nl: Ik wacht onderaan de trap.
example_en: I am waiting at the bottom of the stairs.
alt: Een man staat stil op de vloer bij de eerste trede; de hele trap naast hem is leeg.

scene: one adult sits in the middle of the long bench with both hands in the lap and empty seat left and right, while the other four adults stand inside the house, two at each window, looking out. The front door stands open and the doorway is empty.
must: one person on a long bench, four others still in the house.
avoid: two adults sitting side by side on the bench (met zijn tweeën); five adults squeezed along the bench (met zijn allen); an adult lying on the bench (not the card); an empty bench (not the card).
contrast: Pair with met-zijn-tweeen and met-zijn-allen. The only difference is the number of people: one on the bench here, two or five there.
example_nl: Hij woont in zijn eentje.
example_en: He lives by himself.
alt: Een man zit midden op een lang bankje terwijl vier anderen uit de ramen van het huis kijken.

scene: two adults sit side by side on the bench, shoulders close and turned slightly toward each other, one holding a small paper bag between them, while the other three adults stand inside the house at the two windows. The bench still shows an empty piece at each end.
must: two people close together on the bench, three others still in the house.
avoid: one adult alone on the bench (in zijn eentje); five adults squeezed along the bench (met zijn allen); two adults standing beside the bench (not the card); two adults on separate benches (not the card).
contrast: Pair with in-zijn-eentje and met-zijn-allen. The only difference is the number of people: two on the bench here, one alone or five squeezed there.
example_nl: Wij eten met zijn tweeën.
example_en: The two of us eat.
alt: Een man en een vrouw zitten dicht naast elkaar op een bankje en delen een papieren zak; drie anderen kijken uit het raam.

scene: all five adults squeeze along the bench in one row with no gap, shoulders overlapping, every one smiling. The house behind them stands empty: both windows show an empty room and the open front door shows an empty doorway.
must: five people filling the whole bench, the house behind empty.
avoid: one adult alone on the bench (in zijn eentje); two adults on the bench (met zijn tweeën); five adults standing in a group (not the card); a crowd of fifty (not the card).
contrast: Pair with in-zijn-eentje and met-zijn-tweeen. The only difference is the number of people: five filling the bench here, one alone or two close there.
example_nl: Wij gaan met zijn allen naar het strand.
example_en: We all go to the beach together.
alt: Vijf mensen zitten lachend dicht tegen elkaar op een bankje; het huis achter hen is leeg.

scene: the adult stands on the third of the five stepping stones with the back foot still on it and the front foot reaching toward the fourth stone, arms out for balance and the eyes on the next stone. The first two stones are behind and the fifth lies ahead.
must: a foot reaching from one stone to the next in a row.
avoid: an adult flying above the whole stream with feet off the ground (in één keer); an adult wading through the water (not the card); an adult on a bridge (not the card); an adult walking on a pavement (not the card).
contrast: Pair with in-een-keer. The only difference is the way of crossing: one foot on a stone and the other reaching for the next stone here, both feet in the air over the whole stream there.
example_nl: Zij loopt stap voor stap over de stenen.
example_en: She walks over the stones step by step.
alt: Een man zet zijn voet op de derde van vijf platte stenen in een beek en reikt naar de volgende.

scene: the adult is in mid-air high above the stream with both feet well off the ground and the knees bent, arms stretched out in front, the left bank just behind the back foot and the right bank ahead. The five stepping stones lie untouched below.
must: a person flying over the whole stream, five stones untouched below.
avoid: an adult with one foot on a stone reaching to the next (stap voor stap); an adult jumping on the spot (not the card); an adult diving into the water (not the card); an adult jumping over a fence (not the card).
contrast: Pair with stap-voor-stap. The only difference is the way of crossing: both feet in the air over the whole stream here, one foot on a stone and the other reaching for the next there.
example_nl: Zij springt in één keer over de sloot.
example_en: She jumps over the ditch in one go.
alt: Een vrouw zweeft met gebogen knieën boven een beek terwijl vijf stenen onaangeroerd onder haar liggen.

scene: SKIP: taking turns is alternation over time; one picture cannot show who went first or that the roles will swap.
example_nl: Wij doen het om de beurt.
example_en: We do it in turns.

scene: SKIP: at the same time is only meaningful against another moment; a single picture of two people acting looks the same as any pair.
example_nl: Ze komen precies tegelijk aan.
example_en: They arrive at exactly the same time.

scene: the two adults walk close together, the near hand of one and the near hand of the other clasped together at hip height with the fingers laced, all other arms hanging free and swinging. Both look ahead along the path.
must: two hands clasped together at hip height.
avoid: two adults with a forearm hooked through the other's elbow (arm in arm); two adults walking apart with no contact (not the card); two adults with arms round each other's shoulders (not the card); an adult holding a child's hand (aan de hand lopen).
contrast: Pair with arm-in-arm. The only difference is the link: clasped hands at hip height here, a forearm hooked through the other's elbow there.
example_nl: Zij lopen hand in hand.
example_en: They are walking hand in hand.
alt: Twee mensen lopen naast elkaar en hun vingers zijn in elkaar gevlochten.

scene: the two adults walk close together, the near arm of one bent at the elbow and hooked through the bent elbow of the other so that the forearms rest together at the waist, the free hands relaxed. Both look ahead along the path.
must: an elbow hooked through an elbow at the waist.
avoid: two adults with clasped hands at hip height (hand in hand); two adults walking apart with no contact (not the card); two adults with arms round each other's shoulders (not the card); one adult supporting another who is hurt (not the card).
contrast: Pair with hand-in-hand. The only difference is the link: a forearm hooked through the other's elbow here, clasped hands at hip height there.
example_nl: Het oude paar loopt arm in arm.
example_en: The old couple walks arm in arm.
alt: Twee mensen lopen dicht naast elkaar en haken hun gebogen ellebogen in elkaar.

scene: both feet are bare with five separate toes drawn on each, the ankles and heels visible, and a pair of shoes stands neatly by the wall behind. The adult tiptoes across the floor with a small smile.
must: five bare toes on each foot, shoes left by the wall.
avoid: an adult with ribbed knitted socks on the feet (op sokken); an adult with shoes on (not the card); an adult with sandals (not the card); an adult in a bath (not the card).
contrast: Pair with op-sokken. The only difference is what is on the feet: bare toes here, plain knitted socks with a ribbed cuff there.
example_nl: Zij loopt op blote voeten.
example_en: She walks barefoot.
alt: Een vrouw loopt met zichtbare tenen over een houten vloer, haar schoenen staan bij de muur.

scene: both feet are covered by plain knitted socks with a ribbed cuff at the ankle, no toes visible, and a pair of shoes stands neatly by the wall behind. The adult glides across the floor with a small smile.
must: plain knitted socks with ribbed cuffs, no toes showing.
avoid: an adult with bare toes on the floor (op blote voeten); an adult with slippers (not the card); an adult with shoes on (not the card); an adult in tights (not the card).
contrast: Pair with op-blote-voeten. The only difference is what is on the feet: plain knitted socks here, bare toes there.
example_nl: Hij loopt op sokken door de kamer.
example_en: He walks through the room in his socks.
alt: Een man glijdt in gebreide kousen met een boord over een houten vloer, zijn schoenen staan bij de muur.

scene: the round lamp is screwed to the back wall at eye height on a short bracket and sticks out a hand's length from the wall, a small switch beside it, with a lot of empty wall above it and the ceiling line well above the lamp.
must: a lamp fixed on a bracket to the wall at eye height.
avoid: a lamp hanging on a cord from the ceiling (aan het plafond); a lamp standing on the floor (not the card); a lamp standing on a table (not the card); a framed picture on a wall (not the card).
contrast: Pair with aan-het-plafond. The only difference is where the lamp is fixed: on a bracket at eye height on the wall here, on a cord from the ceiling line there.
example_nl: Het schilderij hangt aan de muur.
example_en: The painting hangs on the wall.
alt: Een lamp zit op ooghoogte op een steunplaatje vast tegen de achterwand van een kamer.

scene: the round lamp hangs from the ceiling line by a short cord, the shade directly below the ceiling and the whole back wall empty beneath it, with a small rose where the cord leaves the ceiling. No bracket or switch is drawn.
must: a lamp hanging on a cord from the ceiling line.
avoid: a lamp fixed to the wall on a bracket (aan de muur); a lamp standing on the floor (not the card); a fan on the ceiling (not the card); a spider hanging from the ceiling (not the card).
contrast: Pair with aan-de-muur. The only difference is where the lamp is fixed: hanging from the ceiling line on a cord here, on a bracket at eye height on the wall there.
example_nl: Er zit een spin aan het plafond.
example_en: There is a spider on the ceiling.
alt: Een lamp hangt aan een kort koord vlak onder de bovenkant van een kamer, met een lege achterwand eronder.

scene: the man wears loose pyjamas with a pattern of thin stripes: a soft buttoned top with a round collar and long loose trousers; his feet are in plain slippers. The coat hook beside him is empty.
must: loose striped pyjamas with a soft round collar.
avoid: a jacket with lapels over a shirt and tie (in pak); a bathrobe with a belt (not the card); a tracksuit (not the card); a person asleep in bed (in bed).
contrast: Pair with in-pak. The only difference is the clothes: loose striped pyjamas here, a jacket with a shirt and tie there.
example_nl: De kinderen ontbijten op zondag in pyjama.
example_en: On Sundays the children have breakfast in their pyjamas.
alt: Een man in losse, gestreepte nachtkleding staat met een mok in de gang.

scene: the man wears a plain dark suit: a jacket with lapels and two buttons done up, a shirt with a collar and a plain tie, long straight trousers; his feet are in plain slippers. The coat hook beside him is empty.
must: a jacket with lapels over a shirt and tie.
avoid: loose striped pyjamas with a round collar (in pyjama); a uniform with a cap and badge (not the card); a coat over a jumper (not the card); a waiter with an apron (not the card).
contrast: Pair with in-pyjama. The only difference is the clothes: a jacket with a shirt and tie here, loose striped pyjamas there.
example_nl: Op de bruiloft komen alle mannen in pak.
example_en: At the wedding all the men come in suits.
alt: Een man in een net jasje met overhemd en stropdas staat met een mok in de gang.

scene: under the pan a full ring of tall flames licks up the sides; the water inside rolls and heaves, large round domes bursting at its surface, and thick curls of steam rise high above the pan. Nothing spills over the rim.
must: tall flames, heaving water and thick steam.
avoid: a tiny flame and almost still water (op een laag pitje); a pan boiling over onto the cooker (not the card); a person stirring a pan (koken, Werkwoorden); a kettle on a hob (not the card).
contrast: Pair with op-een-laag-pitje. The only difference is the heat: tall flames and rolling bubbles here, a tiny flame and almost still water there.
example_nl: Breng het water eerst aan de kook.
example_en: First bring the water to the boil.
alt: Onder een pan water branden hoge vlammen; het water borrelt met grote bellen en er stijgt veel stoom op.

scene: under the pan only a tiny ring of short flames burns, barely visible; the water inside lies almost still, with two or three tiny beads rising and one thin wisp of steam rising from the surface. Nothing spills over the rim.
must: a tiny flame and almost still water.
avoid: tall flames, heaving water and thick steam (aan de kook); a cold pan on a cooker that is off (not the card); a candle flame (not the card); a pan inside an oven (not the card).
contrast: Pair with aan-de-kook. The only difference is the heat: a tiny flame and almost still water here, tall flames and rolling bubbles there.
example_nl: Laat de saus op een laag pitje staan.
example_en: Leave the sauce on a low heat.
alt: Onder een pan water brandt een heel klein vlammetje; het water ligt bijna stil met een dun sliertje stoom.

scene: the casement is pulled into the room only a finger's width, so one thin dark gap runs down its free edge from top to bottom; the rest of the leaf still sits almost flush in the frame, and the handle is turned up.
must: one thin gap down the free edge of an almost shut window.
avoid: the casement swung into the room as far as it goes (wagenwijd open); a window shut flush with no gap (dicht, Bijvoeglijke naamwoorden); a broken pane (not the card); an eye at a narrow gap (kijken door, Voorzetselpaden).
contrast: Pair with wagenwijd-open. The only difference is the casement: in by one thin gap here, swung into the room as far as it goes there.
example_nl: Zet het raam maar op een kier.
example_en: Just leave the window ajar.
alt: Een raam is bijna dicht: er loopt alleen een smalle donkere spleet langs de rand.

scene: the casement is swung into the room as far as its hinges allow and stands at a right angle to the wall, so the whole leaf with its frame and handle shows clearly in front of the wall, and the empty opening beside it shows the sky outside.
must: the whole casement standing into the room at a right angle, the opening clear.
avoid: the casement in by one thin gap (op een kier); a window with the glass missing (not the card); a person climbing through a window (not the card); a door swung wide (open, Bijvoeglijke naamwoorden).
contrast: Pair with op-een-kier. The only difference is the casement: swung into the room as far as it goes here, in by one thin gap there.
example_nl: Bij deze hitte staan alle ramen wagenwijd open.
example_en: In this heat all the windows are wide open.
alt: Een raamvleugel is helemaal naar binnen gedraaid en staat haaks op de muur, zodat je door het hele kozijn de lucht ziet.
